q: Under Sec. 32.02, is Owner insurance against contingent liability for personal injury/death arising from the Contract's operations mandatory or optional for the Owner?
o: Optional — the Owner may, at his option, maintain such insurance
Prohibited, as this coverage duplicates the Contractor's insurance
Mandatory only for projects over Php 5,000,000
n: Sec. 32.02 (Owner's Optional Insurance) makes this coverage optional, at the Owner's election. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 32, Sec. 32.02)

q: Under Sec. 22.02, how frequently, at most, may the Contractor submit a Request for Payment for work done?
o: Not more than once a month
n: Sec. 22.02 (Requests for Payment) allows the Contractor to submit a Request for Payment periodically but not more than once a month. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.02)

q: Under Art. 15's closing provision (numbered 15.01 in that section, following 15.11), removal of all temporary work erected by the Contractor and cleaning of the premises is required as a condition for:
o: Release of the Performance Bond only
Completing the work and its acceptance by the Owner
Submission of the Schedule of Completion
n: The closing clause of Art. 15 (Removal of Temporary Structures) requires the Contractor to remove all temporary work and clean the premises as a condition for completing the work and before the Owner's acceptance. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 15 (Removal of Temporary Structures))

q: Per Sec. 2.03(c), who bears responsibility for the adequacy of the design and sufficiency of the Drawings and Specifications?
n: Sec. 2.03(c) places responsibility for adequacy of design and sufficiency of Drawings/Specifications on the Owner (through the Architect/Engineer as representative). (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 2, Sec. 2.03(c))

q: If the Architect fails to render a decision within how many days after the parties have presented their evidence, may either party then demand arbitration, per Sec. 33.04(d)?
n: Sec. 33.04(d) allows either party to demand arbitration if the Architect fails to render a decision within fifteen (15) days after the parties have presented their evidence. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 33, Sec. 33.04(d))

q: If the Owner fails to timely pay an approved Request for Payment, Sec. 22.07 subjects the unpaid amount to:
o: A doubling of the amount due as a penalty
Payment of interest based on banking loan rates prevailing at the time of signing the Contract
n: Sec. 22.07 provides that the Owner's failure to pay is subject to interest based on prevailing banking loan rates at the time the Contract was signed. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.07)

q: In an emergency affecting the safety of life, the work, or adjoining property, Art. 18 permits the Contractor to:
o: Suspend all work immediately and evacuate the site
Act at his discretion, without special instruction or authorization, to prevent threatened loss or injury
Do nothing until the Board of Arbitration convenes
Act only after obtaining the Architect's or Owner's written authorization
n: Art. 18 (Sec. 18.01) authorizes the Contractor to act at his discretion in an emergency, without waiting for special instructions, to prevent loss or injury. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 18, Sec. 18.01)

q: Before submitting its bid, a Contractor notices what it believes is a conflict between two Specifications sections but does NOT ask the Architect for a written decision before submitting its proposal. If, after the contract is awarded, the Contractor performs the less expensive of the two possible methods, what happens under Sec. 3.03(a)?
o: The Contractor is deemed to have estimated the MORE expensive method, and must credit the Owner the difference between the more expensive and less expensive work
The Owner must pay extra for the discrepancy
Nothing — the Contractor is free to choose either method after award
n: Sec. 3.03(a): absent a pre-bid written decision from the Architect, the Contractor is deemed to have estimated the more expensive way of doing the work; if the less expensive method is used after award, the Contractor must credit the Owner the difference. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 3, Sec. 3.03(a))

q: Under Art. 34(c), in interpreting the Contract and judging its performance, whose side must the Architect take?
o: The Contractor's side, to protect the party doing the physical work
Whichever side offers the more reasonable technical argument at the time
Neither side — the Architect shall side with neither the Owner nor the Contractor, using his powers to enforce faithful performance by both
The Owner's side, since the Architect is hired by the Owner
n: Art. 34(c) requires the Architect, as interpreter of the Contract and judge of its performance, to side with neither party but to enforce faithful performance by both. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 34(c))

q: Per Sec. 22.13(a), the Contractor remains liable to remedy defects due to faulty materials or workmanship (and pay for resulting damage) if such defects appear within what period from the date of acceptance of the work by the Owner, notwithstanding final payment?
n: Sec. 22.13(a) (Correction of Work After Final Payment) fixes this liability period at one year from the date of acceptance of the work by the Owner. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.13(a))

q: A civil works Contractor's uncovered work is re-examined by the Architect for suspected non-conformance, but it turns out the work actually meets Contract requirements. Under Sec. 20.03(d), besides an appropriate time extension, what compensation is the Contractor entitled to for the cost of labor and materials involved in the examination and replacement?
o: The actual cost with no allowance
No compensation, as re-examination is a normal risk of the trade
n: Sec. 20.03(d) provides that if examined work is found to meet Contract requirements, the actual cost of labor and materials plus 15 percent shall be allowed the Contractor, along with a time extension if completion was delayed. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.03(d))

q: Under Sec. 5.05, how many sets of prints of shop drawings must the Contractor submit to the Architect for approval, and in what form must resubmissions of disapproved drawings be made?
o: Five sets initially; no resubmission allowed
Three sets initially; resubmissions in duplicate until approved
Two sets initially; resubmissions in triplicate
One set initially; resubmissions as a single original
n: Sec. 5.05 requires three sets of prints of shop drawings for approval; Sec. 5.05(a) requires corrected shop drawings to be resubmitted in duplicate until the Architect's approval is obtained. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 5, Sec. 5.05)

q: Section XI (Schedule of Time Limits) is described in the General Conditions as:
o: A separate, legally distinct contract from the General Conditions
An appendix that supersedes all Article time limits if there is any conflict
An indexed summary section, based on the entire General Conditions, provided to facilitate the Contractor's execution of the work by consolidating its various time limits
A section applicable only to government-funded projects
n: The introduction to Section XI states it is an indexed section, based on the entire General Conditions, provided to facilitate execution of the Contractor's work by consolidating time limits from the various Articles. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Section XI (Schedule of Time Limits), introductory note)

q: If the Contractor's work depends on the proper execution of another (separate) contractor's work and the Contractor fails to inspect and report defects in that work, Sec. 24.03 provides that this failure:
o: Voids the Contractor's own portion of the Contract
Constitutes an acceptance of the other contractor's work as fit and proper for receiving the Contractor's own work (except for later-developing defects)
Automatically shifts liability to the Owner
n: Sec. 24.03 provides that failure to inspect and report defects in a separate contractor's work is deemed an acceptance of that work as fit for the Contractor's own subsequent work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 24, Sec. 24.03)

q: Under Sec. 20.07(a), changes ordered by the Owner (altering, adding to, or deducting from the work) must be:
o: Ordered in writing, with no change/omission considered authorized without written instructions signed by the Owner
Approved by the Contractor's Surety before being valid
Verbal, but later confirmed within 30 days
Limited to no more than 5% of contract value
n: Sec. 20.07(a) requires Owner-ordered changes to be in writing; no change/omission is considered authorized without the Owner's signed written instructions. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.07(a))

q: Under Sec. 7.01, who is generally responsible for securing and paying for construction permits and licenses necessary for the work?
o: The Contractor, though costs may be reimbursed by the Owner if specifically stipulated
n: Sec. 7.01 places the duty of securing permits/licenses and paying required fees on the Contractor, with possible Owner reimbursement only if stipulated in prior instructions. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 7, Sec. 7.01)

q: Under UAP Doc. 301, the Contract Documents consist of five enumerated items. Which of the following completes that list: Agreement, General Conditions, Special Provisions, Specifications, and ___?
n: Sec. 1.01 enumerates the Contract Documents as: (a) Agreement, (b) General Conditions, (c) Special Provisions, (d) Specifications, (e) Drawings. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.01)

q: Under Sec. 26.03, is a decision by the Architect a condition precedent to arbitration between the Contractor and a Sub-contractor?
o: No — a decision by the Architect shall not be a condition precedent to arbitration in Contractor-Sub-contractor disputes
n: Sec. 26.03 provides that between the Contractor and Sub-contractor, an Architect's decision need not be a condition precedent to arbitration, unlike the general rule for Owner-Contractor disputes. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 26, Sec. 26.03)

q: The Contractor notifies the Architect of Owner-caused delay (e.g., late Owner-supplied materials). Per Sec. 20.08, within how many days after recognizing such delay must the Contractor give written notice in order to preserve a valid claim for extra cost?
n: Sec. 20.08 requires written notice within fifteen days after recognition of a delay attributable to the Owner, or no claim shall be valid. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.08)

q: If a revision or amendment to laws, ordinances, regulations or building codes made DURING the construction period affects the cost or time of completion of the Contract, Art. 8 (General, Equipment and Materials) provides that:
o: The Contractor absorbs the added cost with no adjustment
The Owner may terminate the Contract immediately
A corresponding adjustment shall be made
The Architect alone decides with no recourse for either party
n: Art. 8 provides that where a legal revision made during construction affects cost or time, a corresponding adjustment shall be made to the Contract. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 8)

q: A construction firm is bidding on a UAP-301-governed project. Under Sec. 1.11 and 1.12, what percentage of the Contract amount must its Performance Bond and Payment Bond each be, and when must they be furnished?
o: 10% each, furnished after award of the Certificate of Completion
15% each, furnished prior to (before) the execution of the Contract
30% each, furnished within 15 days of Notice to Proceed
n: Secs. 1.11-1.12 (confirmed at Sec. 31.03) require a Performance Bond and a Payment Bond each equal to 15% of the Contract amount, furnished before execution of the Contract. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Secs. 1.11-1.12; Art. 31, Sec. 31.03)

q: After terminating the Contract and taking over the work, per Sec. 29.04, the full extent of damages recoverable from the original Contractor and/or his sureties includes:
o: Only liquidated damages, with no recovery of excess completion cost allowed
Only the excess completion cost over the Contract Price

Total daily liquidated damages up to the day before takeover, PLUS the excess cost of completion over the Contract Price (including added architectural/managerial/administrative and supervision costs)
Nothing, since termination waives all further claims
n: Sec. 29.04 entitles the Owner to recover both (a) accrued daily liquidated damages up to takeover and (b) the excess cost of completing the project over the Contract Price, including added professional/administrative costs. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 29, Sec. 29.04)

q: Under Sec. 21.02, Contract Time computation commences on which day counted from receipt of the Notice to Proceed (NTP), unless otherwise stipulated?
n: Sec. 21.02 provides that computation of Contract Time commences on the seventh (7th) day from receipt of the Notice to Proceed, unless otherwise stipulated, with every calendar day thereafter counted as a working day. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 21, Sec. 21.02)

q: Per Sec. 10.03(b), when may a substitution be made for a material, article, or process specified exclusively by trade name?
o: Only with the written approval of the Architect
Only with verbal approval of the Project Representative
Freely, as long as the substitute is cheaper
n: Sec. 10.03(b) allows substitution of a specified trade-name material only with the Architect's written approval. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 10, Sec. 10.03(b))

q:
Which pair of terms is correctly matched to their UAP Doc. 301 definitions?
(1) General Conditions — printed documents stipulating the procedural and administrative aspects of the contract.
(2) Special Provisions — instructions issued prior to bidding to supplement/modify Drawings, Specifications and/or General Conditions.
n: Sec. 1.19 defines General Conditions and Sec. 1.20 defines Special Provisions exactly as stated in both (1) and (2). (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Secs. 1.19-1.20)

q: Under Sec. 31.01 (Contractor's Liability Insurance), the Contractor's liability insurance policy must contain a clause providing that it cannot be cancelled by the insurer without how many days' written notice to the Owner of intention to cancel?
n: Sec. 31.01 requires the liability insurance policy to provide that it will not be cancelled without ten (10) days' written notice to the Owner. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 31, Sec. 31.01)

q: The Contractor plans to temporarily suspend work (not due to an accident) to redeploy equipment. Per Sec. 21.04(f), how many days' advance written notice must be given to the Architect before suspending the work?
n: Sec. 21.04(f) requires the Contractor to give the Architect written notice at least ten (10) days prior to beginning, suspending (except in case of accident), or resuming work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 21, Sec. 21.04(f))
scenario: A building Contractor receives its Notice to Proceed (NTP) dated March 1 for a project governed by UAP Doc. 301. Various contract-administration deadlines under Art. 21 (Time of Completion) must now be tracked from that date.

q: Materials furnished by the Owner (Art. 11) are, by the mere fact that the Owner furnishes them, considered:
o: Conclusive evidence of their acceptability for the intended purpose
Subject to further testing before any use
n: Art. 11 provides that the Owner furnishing the material is conclusive evidence of its acceptability for the intended purpose, and the Contractor may continue to use it until otherwise directed. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 11)

q: A sudden but very light drizzle causes a minor, easily-repaired delay on site. Under Sec. 1.26 (Act of God or Force Majeure), can the Contractor claim reparation for damages from this event?
o: No — rain, wind, flood or other natural phenomenon of inconsequential degree for the locality is not considered an Act of God, and no reparation is due
Yes, but only if it lasts more than one hour
Yes, any rain automatically qualifies as Force Majeure
No, because Force Majeure is never a valid Contractor defense under this Contract
n: Sec. 1.26 expressly excludes natural phenomena of inconsequential degree for the locality from the definition of Act of God/Force Majeure, so no reparation is made to the Contractor for resulting damage. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.26)

q: Per Sec. 31.05(d), once notified in writing of defective work developing during the guarantee/warranty period, within how many days must the Contractor make the necessary repairs, at his own cost?
n: Sec. 31.05(d) requires the Contractor to complete repairs and corrective work within five (5) days after written notice from the Owner, at his own cost. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 31, Sec. 31.05(d))

q: A Contractor's Breakdown of Work and Corresponding Value must be submitted within how many days from receipt of the Notice to Proceed, per Sec. 22.01?
n: Sec. 22.01 requires the Contractor to submit the complete Breakdown of Work and Corresponding Value within fifteen (15) days from receipt of the Notice to Proceed. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.01)

q: Under Sec. 15.01, the temporary office the Contractor must provide must include, among other things, one room for the Architect's use of approximately what floor area?
n: Sec. 15.01 (Temporary Office and Contractor's Building) requires one room of approximately 12 square meters to be provided for the Architect's use. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 15, Sec. 15.01)

q: How many copies of the Contract Documents must be signed by the Owner and the Contractor, duly witnessed, under Art. 2 of the General Conditions?
n: Sec. 2.01 requires the Contract Documents to be signed in quintuplicate (five copies) by the Owner and Contractor, duly witnessed. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 2, Sec. 2.01)

q: Under Sec. 33.01 (Liens), before final payment (or any part of the retained percentage) becomes due, the Contractor may, if a sub-contractor refuses to furnish a lien release or receipt in full, instead:
o: Furnish a bond satisfactory to the Owner to indemnify him against any lien
Ask the Owner to sue the sub-contractor directly
Simply proceed to final payment without any remedy
Withhold payment from that sub-contractor indefinitely
n: Sec. 33.01 allows the Contractor to furnish an indemnity bond satisfactory to the Owner in lieu of a lien release/receipt when a sub-contractor refuses to furnish one. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 33, Sec. 33.01)

q: Per Sec. 22.03(a), what size must the progress photographs accompanying each Request for Payment be, how many exposures are taken each period, and how many prints delivered?
o: 6"x8" photos; four exposures (one per side of the building); eight prints (2 copies each)
n: Sec. 22.03(a) requires 6"x8" photographs, four exposures (one on each side of the building) per period, and eight prints (2 copies of each exposure) delivered to the Architect. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.03(a))

q: Per Sec. 16.01(a), who must the Contractor provide to guard the site and premises from the commencement of operations until the building is fully completed?
o: A licensed security agency under contract with the Owner
No guard is required if the site is fenced
Reliable and competent watchmen, under the Contractor's control
n: Sec. 16.01(a) requires the Contractor to provide reliable and competent watchmen to guard the site from commencement until full completion. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 16, Sec. 16.01(a))

q: Upon completion of the work and before Final Payment, what must the Contractor do with the Drawings, Specifications and Models furnished by the Architect, per Sec. 2.05?
o: Keep them permanently as the Contractor's property
Return them to the Architect (except the signed contract set), as they remain the Architect's property
n: Sec. 2.05 states the Drawings, Specifications, and Models (with additional instructions) are the property of the Architect and, except the signed contract set, must be returned to the Architect before Final Payment. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 2, Sec. 2.05)

q: Per Sec. 33.05(b), how is a formal Board of Arbitration composed, and what vote is required for its decisions?
o: The Owner and Contractor each appoint one member, and those two members appoint a third who acts as chairman; decisions require only a simple majority
A single arbitrator chosen by the Owner; unanimous vote required
Five members appointed entirely by the Architect; two-thirds vote required
A panel of licensed architects only; unanimous vote required
n: Sec. 33.05(b) describes a three-member Board (one appointed by each party, plus a jointly-appointed chairman), with decisions requiring only a simple majority. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 33, Sec. 33.05(b))

q: A Contractor has now billed 68% of a Contract Price. Under Sec. 22.09, since this exceeds 65%, what document must the Contractor submit before any further payment on the excess may be made?
o: A sworn statement (before an officer authorized to administer oaths) that all bills for labor and materials have been duly paid by the Contractor and Sub-contractors, except those enumerated
A certificate from the Bureau of Internal Revenue
n: Sec. 22.09 (Payments Over 65 Percent) requires a sworn statement that all labor and material bills have been duly paid, except bills specifically enumerated as unpaid, before payment on contracts exceeding 65% of the Contract Price. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.09)
scenario: On a building contract governed by UAP Doc. 301, a Contractor's cumulative billings have just crossed the 65% threshold of the total Contract Price, triggering the special payment safeguard in Sec. 22.09.

q: If the Contractor supervises the work personally rather than through an employed engineer/architect, Sec. 19.02 requires the Contractor personally to be:
o: Any individual approved by the local government
A civil engineer with 10 years' experience specifically
n: Sec. 19.02 requires that if the Contractor personally supervises the work, he must be a licensed engineer or architect; otherwise he must employ one acceptable to the Architect, who must inspect the site at least once a week. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 19, Sec. 19.02)

q: In case of discrepancy in figures or drawings discovered during construction, Sec. 3.04 requires that the matter be:
o: Submitted immediately to the Architect before any adjustment is made, otherwise at the Contractor's own risk and expense
Ignored unless it affects more than 5% of the work
Resolved directly between the Contractor and Sub-contractor
n: Sec. 3.04 (Discrepancies in Drawings) requires immediate submission to the Architect before any adjustment, or the Contractor bears the risk and expense. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 3, Sec. 3.04)

q: Per Art. 35(a), who is solely responsible for the Engineers' own designs, computations, and professional services rendered in preparing the Drawings and Specifications?
n: Art. 35(a) makes the Engineers solely responsible for their own respective designs, computations, and professional services. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 35(a))

q: Under Sec. 22.14 (Release of Retention), the amount retained by the Owner is released within how long after the date of final payment?
n: Sec. 22.14 requires the retention amount to be released within three months after the date of final payment. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.14)

q: A Php 20,000,000 contract's actual quantities of excavation work overran the Proposal's stated quantities. Per Sec. 20.06, up to what percentage of overrun or underrun from the Proposal quantities is treated as a normal, expected margin of adjustment NOT requiring a change in Contract Price?
n: Sec. 20.06 (Increased or Decreased Quantities of Work) treats overruns/underruns up to five percent (5%) of Proposal quantities as a normal margin of adjustment not changing the Contract Price. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.06)
scenario: A Contractor is executing a Php 20,000,000 lump-sum building contract under UAP Doc. 301. During construction, several quantity and cost adjustments become necessary and are being evaluated against the General Conditions' rules on changes, extra work, and time extensions.

q: Submission of shop drawings must be accompanied by a letter of transmittal, per Sec. 5.04, in what form?
o: No letter of transmittal is required
n: Sec. 5.04 requires shop drawing submissions to be accompanied by a letter of transmittal in duplicate. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 5, Sec. 5.04)

q: Cross-checking the Schedule of Time Limits against Art. 33, a Contractor and Owner have been unable to resolve a factual dispute, and the Architect has not rendered a decision despite the parties having presented their evidence. According to both Sec. 33.04(d) and Item 8 of the Schedule of Time Limits, after how many days of the Architect's inaction may either party demand arbitration?
n: Both Sec. 33.04(d) and Item 8 of the Schedule of Time Limits confirm that either party may demand arbitration if the Architect fails to decide within fifteen (15) days after the parties present their evidence. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Section XI, Item 8; Art. 33, Sec. 33.04(d))

q: Per Sec. 25.01 (General), may the ENTIRE work called for by the Contract be sublet or sub-contracted?
o: Only if the Owner is a government entity
Yes, but only with Architect approval
No — the entire work shall not be sublet or sub-contracted, though any part or specialty work may be, subject to Sec. 25.02
n: Sec. 25.01 prohibits subletting/sub-contracting the ENTIRE work, while allowing any part or specialty work to be sublet subject to the competency-evaluation provisions of Sec. 25.02. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 25, Sec. 25.01)

q: Under Sec. 20.07(f), what kind of changes may the Architect (as opposed to the Owner) order directly, in giving instructions?
o: Minor changes in the work, not involving extra cost and not inconsistent with the design concept of the building
Any change regardless of cost impact
Only changes reducing the contract price
Changes to the Contract Time only
n: Sec. 20.07(f) (Changes Ordered by the Architect) limits the Architect's unilateral authority to minor changes not involving extra cost and consistent with the design concept. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.07(f))

q: Per Sec. 7.03, who is responsible for the establishment of lot lines, boundary lines, easements, and benchmarks (by a certified surveyor), unless this responsibility is relegated (at the Owner's cost) to the Contractor?
n: Sec. 7.03 (Construction Stakes and Reference Marks) makes the Owner responsible for establishing lot lines, boundary lines, easements, and benchmarks via a certified surveyor, unless relegated to the Contractor at the Owner's cost. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 7, Sec. 7.03)

q: In UAP Doc. 301, who is defined as the party "ordering the project for execution, including duly appointed successors, or authorized representatives"?
n: Sec. 1.02 defines the Owner as the person or entity ordering the project for execution, including successors or authorized representatives. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.02)

q: A public authority's court order stops a Contractor's work entirely, through no fault of the Contractor, for 95 consecutive days. Per Sec. 27(a), has this triggered the Contractor's right to suspend or terminate the Contract?
o: Yes — a court/public-authority-ordered stoppage exceeding ninety (90) days through no fault of the Contractor is one ground to suspend or terminate, upon 15 days' written notice
No, only stoppages exceeding 180 days qualify
Yes, but only after a full year of stoppage
No, only an Owner-caused stoppage counts
n: Art. 27(a) allows the Contractor to suspend or terminate (upon 15 days' written notice) if a court or public authority order stops the work for 90 days through no fault of the Contractor; 95 days satisfies this. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 27(a))
scenario: A Contractor governed by UAP Doc. 301 is evaluating whether recent events on its project give it grounds under Art. 27 to suspend work or terminate the Contract, each requiring the appropriate written notice period.

q: A Contractor's building project has reached the point where the value of the work completed is 96% of the contract amount, with only minor items remaining. Under Sec. 20.11, has the Contractor achieved "Substantial Completion"?
o: No, Substantial Completion always requires 100% completion
Yes, because only minor items remain, regardless of percentage
No — Substantial Completion requires the value of work completed to be not less than 98% of the contract amount, with only minor unfinished work remaining
n: Sec. 20.11 defines Substantial Completion as the value of work completed being not less than 98% of the contract amount and the remaining unfinished work being minor. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.11)

q: Under Sec. 9.01, referring to certain equipment in the Specifications by brand name and catalogue number is meant to:
o: Eliminate all other manufacturers from consideration
Establish standards of quality, without eliminating other products of equal or better quality from competition where fully suitable in design
Require Owner approval only, bypassing the Architect and Engineer
Bind the Contractor to that single brand with no substitution allowed under any circumstance
n: Sec. 9.01 clarifies that naming equipment by brand/catalogue number establishes quality standards but does not eliminate other suitable products from competition, subject to substitution procedures. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 9, Sec. 9.01)

q: A Contractor has just had its 15% Performance Bond and 15% Payment Bond released by the Owner. Per the General Conditions, what must it furnish next, and at what percentage of the Contract Price?
o: A Proposal Bond equal to 5% of the Contract Price
A Guaranteed (Guarantee) Bond equal to 30% of the Contract Price
A second Performance Bond equal to 20%
n: Sec. 1.13 (and Sec. 31.04) defines the Guaranteed Bond, furnished at 30% of the Total Contract Cost, given only after the Performance and Payment Bonds are released, to guarantee quality of materials and workmanship. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.13; Art. 31, Sec. 31.04)

q: Per Sec. 29.03(b), after termination, may the Contractor recover any amount for prospective profits on work done after the termination of the Contract?
o: Only if the Owner completes the project through the same Contractor's former Sub-contractors
Yes, at the same rate as the original contract
No — no claim for prospective profits on work done after termination shall be considered or allowed
n: Sec. 29.03(b) bars any claim for prospective profits on work performed after the Contract's termination. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 29, Sec. 29.03(b))

q: A Contractor receives its Notice to Proceed on March 1. Per Sec. 21.02, on what date does Contract Time computation begin (absent any other stipulation)?
n: Since Contract Time computation commences on the 7th day from receipt of NTP, counting from March 1, the 7th day is March 8. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 21, Sec. 21.02)
scenario: A building Contractor receives its Notice to Proceed (NTP) dated March 1 for a project governed by UAP Doc. 301. Various contract-administration deadlines under Art. 21 (Time of Completion) must now be tracked from that date.

q: Who bears the cost of shipment, delivery, handling, and testing of material samples submitted for testing, per Sec. 10.04?
n: Sec. 10.04 (Testing Samples of Materials) places all costs for shipment, delivery, handling, and testing of samples on the Contractor. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 10, Sec. 10.04)

q: Under the General Conditions, "written or printed description of the work to be done, describing qualities of material and mode of construction" defines which document?
o: Breakdown of Work and Corresponding Value
n: Sec. 1.21 defines Specifications in exactly these terms, distinct from Drawings (graphical presentations, Sec. 1.18). (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.21)

q: A Contractor on a Php 8,000,000 project is preparing its Performance Bond and Payment Bond as required by Sec. 31.03, prior to signing the Contract. What amount must EACH bond be worth?
n: Sec. 31.03 requires a Performance Bond equal to 15% of the Contract amount and a separate 15% Payment Bond: 15% of Php 8,000,000 = Php 1,200,000 each. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 31, Sec. 31.03)
scenario: A Contractor has been awarded a Php 8,000,000 building contract under UAP Doc. 301. Before signing the Contract, it must post the bonds required under Art. 31, and later replace them per that Article's sequence.

q: Per Sec. 21.04(b), what must accompany any Contractor request for an extension of time, before it is submitted to the Owner for consideration?
o: Proof of payment of all sub-contractors
The written consent of the Bondsmen
n: Sec. 21.04(b) requires the written consent of the bondsmen to be attached to any Contractor request for extension of time. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 21, Sec. 21.04(b))

q: Under Art. 12 (Royalties and Patents), who is responsible for paying royalties and license fees on patented materials and processes the Contractor furnishes, and for defending infringement suits?
n: Art. 12 requires the Contractor to pay all royalties and license fees on patented materials/processes he furnishes, defend related suits, and hold the Owner harmless. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 12)

q: Which of the following word-definitions from Art. 1 is INCORRECTLY paired?
o: "Provide" — to merely deliver materials to the jobsite without installing them
"Furnish" — purchase and/or fabricate and deliver to the jobsite
"Install" — to build in, mount to position, connect or apply an object specified, ready for use
n: Secs. 1.30-1.32 define Furnish, Install, and Provide (= furnish AND install); choice (d) misstates Provide, which by definition includes installation, not delivery alone. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Secs. 1.30-1.32)

q: Per Sec. 31.05(c), the Contractor's guaranty/warranty for materials and workmanship runs, absent a longer specified period, for how long, measured from the date of the final certificate?
n: Sec. 31.05(c) sets the default guaranty/warranty period at one year (or longer if the Specifications provide), from the date of the final certificate issued by the Architect. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 31, Sec. 31.05(c))

q: A Request for Payment covering Php 3,000,000 of work accomplished (on a project where the Contract is only 30% complete overall) is submitted under Sec. 22.02. What retention percentage applies, absent any other agreement?
n: Sec. 22.02 provides that each Request for Payment is computed less a 10% retention (unless otherwise agreed), until 50% of the Contract has been accomplished. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.02)
scenario: A Contractor is billing progress payments on a Php 10,000,000 building contract governed by UAP Doc. 301. At the time of a given billing, the Contract's cumulative percentage of completion determines what retention rules and payment procedures apply.

q: Per Sec. 15.06, how many painted signs may the Contractor erect on the project (naming the Architect, Contractor, and sub-contractors), and who must approve its size, color, lettering, and location?
o: One sign, subject to the Architect's approval
As many as desired, no approval needed
None are allowed under any circumstance
Two signs, subject to the Owner's approval
n: Sec. 15.06 (Temporary Signs) allows the Contractor to erect one painted sign as approved by the Architect, who approves its size, color, lettering, and location. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 15, Sec. 15.06)

q: The Drawings and Specifications for a project conflict with each other on a detail, and separately, the General Conditions conflicts with the detailed specifications on another point. Per Sec. 2.03(a), how are these two conflicts resolved?
o: The Architect must always issue a Change Order to resolve any conflict
Specifications control over Drawings; detailed specifications requirements control over the General Conditions
The General Conditions always control over any other document
In both cases, the Drawings control
n: Sec. 2.03(a): where Drawings and Specifications vary, Specifications control; where General Conditions conflict with detailed specifications requirements, the detailed specifications control. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 2, Sec. 2.03(a))

q: Per Sec. 33.02(a), may the Contractor assign the Contract in whole or in part, or sublet any part of the work, without consent?
o: No, this is absolutely prohibited even with Owner consent
No — this requires the prior written consent of the Owner, and such consent does not relieve the Contractor of full responsibility and liability for the work
Yes, provided the Architect is notified afterward
n: Sec. 33.02(a) requires the Owner's prior written consent for assignment or subletting, and even with consent the Contractor remains fully responsible and liable for the work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 33, Sec. 33.02(a))

q: Within how many days after receipt of a Request for Payment must the Architect either issue a Certificate of Payment or withhold the Request, per Sec. 22.04?
n: Sec. 22.04 requires the Architect to act (issue a Certificate of Payment or withhold it, with written reasons) within fifteen (15) days after receipt of a Request for Payment. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.04)

q: Trees and plants that need to be transplanted, per Sec. 16.03(a), are done by the Contractor at his own expense if they are located within how many meters from the building lines?
n: Sec. 16.03(a) requires the Contractor, at his own expense, to transplant trees and plants that need to be relocated within fifty (50) meters from the building lines. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 16, Sec. 16.03(a))

q: How many sets of Drawings and Specifications must the Owner furnish the Contractor free of charge, under Sec. 3.01?
n: Sec. 3.01 requires the Owner to furnish the Contractor three sets of Drawings and Specifications free of charge; additional copies are at the Contractor's cost of reproduction. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 3, Sec. 3.01)

q: Per Sec. 33.05(c), is the decision of the arbitrators a condition precedent to a party's right to pursue legal action against the other?
o: Only if the Architect consents to skip arbitration
No, either party may sue directly at any time
Yes — it is mutually agreed that the arbitrators' decision is a condition precedent to any right of legal action
n: Sec. 33.05(c) makes the arbitrators' decision a condition precedent to either party's right of legal action against the other. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 33, Sec. 33.05(c))

q: Per Sec. 22.10, if the Contractor fails to pay for the removal of condemned work within ten days after the Owner removes it, what may the Owner do after a further ten days' written notice?
o: Sell the removed materials at auction or private sale and account for the net proceeds after deducting costs
File a criminal complaint against the Contractor
Deduct double the amount from the next payment as a penalty
n: Sec. 22.10 allows the Owner, upon the Contractor's failure to pay removal expenses within 10 days, to sell the condemned materials at auction or private sale (after a further 10 days' written notice) and account for net proceeds. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.10)

q: A supervising engineer employed by the Contractor (in lieu of the Contractor personally supervising) must inspect the site at least how often, per Sec. 19.02?
n: Sec. 19.02 requires the licensed engineer or architect acceptable to the Architect to supervise the work personally and inspect at least once a week. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 19, Sec. 19.02)

q: Under Sec. 4.01, additional detail drawings and instructions issued by the Architect during construction are to be treated, in terms of contractual force, as:
o: Valid only if signed by the Owner personally
Advisory only, with no binding effect
Of equal force as those originally accompanying the specifications
n: Sec. 4.01 states such additional drawings/instructions are considered of equal force as those originally accompanying the specifications. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 4, Sec. 4.01)

q: Under Art. 36 (Sec. 36.03), if a dispute arises between a Project Representative/Resident Engineer/Construction Inspector and the Contractor over materials or the work, what authority do these on-site representatives have?
o: Authority to modify the Contract Price without Architect approval
Authority to unilaterally terminate the Contract
Authority to reject materials or suspend the work until the issue is referred to and decided by the Architect
None — only the Architect may act, with no interim authority for the representative
n: Sec. 36.03 grants Project Representatives/Resident Engineers/Construction Inspectors authority to reject materials or suspend work pending the Architect's decision on the disputed issue. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 36, Sec. 36.03)

q: A Contractor accomplishes Php 2,500,000 worth of work in a given billing period on a contract still below the 50% completion threshold, with a 10% retention applying and no previous unpaid balance for that item. Rounding to the nearest peso, what net amount (before any other deductions) will the Architect certify for payment on this billing?
n: Per Sec. 22.02, a 10% retention is deducted: Php 2,500,000 x (1 - 0.10) = Php 2,250,000 net of retention. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.02)
scenario: A Contractor is billing progress payments on a Php 10,000,000 building contract governed by UAP Doc. 301. At the time of a given billing, the Contract's cumulative percentage of completion determines what retention rules and payment procedures apply.

q: Using the same Php 20,000,000 contract, the Owner orders extra work valued using actual direct cost. Per Sec. 20.07(d)(3), what percentage is added to the actual direct cost of the extra work to cover the Contractor's profit, overhead, and contractor's tax?
n: Sec. 20.07(d)(3) allows actual direct cost PLUS Fifteen Percent (15%) for the Contractor's profit, overhead, and contractor's tax as one method of valuing extra work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.07(d)(3))
scenario: A Contractor is executing a Php 20,000,000 lump-sum building contract under UAP Doc. 301. During construction, several quantity and cost adjustments become necessary and are being evaluated against the General Conditions' rules on changes, extra work, and time extensions.

q: The Architect approves a Contractor's shop drawings "in general." Under Sec. 5.06, does this approval relieve the Contractor of responsibility for the accuracy of those shop drawings?
o: Yes, but only for structural shop drawings
Yes, approval fully transfers responsibility to the Architect
No, unless the Owner co-signs the approval

No — approval does not relieve the Contractor of responsibility for accuracy, proper fitting, or errors, unless deviations were specifically called to the Architect's attention in writing and approved
n: Sec. 5.06 (Responsibility for Accuracy) makes clear that general approval of shop drawings does not relieve the Contractor of responsibility for accuracy or deviations unless specifically flagged in writing and approved. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 5, Sec. 5.06)

q: A project's overall purpose and scope, as reflected across UAP Doc. 301's eleven Sections, is best described as governing the relationship and procedural/administrative rules among which three parties principally?
o: Only the Architect and the Engineer
Only the Owner and the local government building official
The Owner, the Architect, and the Contractor (with Engineers and Project Representatives as supporting roles)
n: Across its eleven Sections, UAP Doc. 301's General Conditions govern the procedural and administrative relationship principally among the Owner, the Architect, and the Contractor, with Engineers and Project Representatives assisting the Architect. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, General Conditions (overall structure, Sections I-XI))

q: Per Sec. 25.02, at least how many days prior to the date of bidding must the Contractor seek the Architect's clarification on which areas of work require sub-contractor competency evaluation?
n: Sec. 25.02 requires the Contractor to seek this clarification at least fifteen (15) days prior to the bidding date, then submit a list of prospective sub-contractors for approval. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 25, Sec. 25.02)

q: Any claim for adjustment involving questions of fact arising from a change order must be asserted within how many days from the date the change is ordered, per Sec. 20.07(e)?
n: Sec. 20.07(e) requires claims for adjustment involving questions of fact to be asserted within fifteen (15) days from the date the change is ordered, unless the Architect extends this for proper cause. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.07(e))

q: Under Sec. 7.03(b), in how many widely separated places must the Contractor establish benchmarks?
o: At least two widely separated places
At every floor only, with no ground-level requirement
n: Sec. 7.03(b) requires the Contractor to establish benchmarks in not less than two widely separated places, in addition to establishing benchmarks at each floor as work progresses. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 7, Sec. 7.03(b))

q: The Project Representative, as defined in the General Conditions, is best described as:
o: The licensed engineer who designs the structural system
The full-time Construction Inspector hired by the Owner and duly authorized to assist the Architect and Engineer in supervision
A member of the Board of Arbitration
The Contractor's project engineer stationed on site
n: Sec. 1.05 defines the Project Representative as the full-time Construction Inspector hired by the Owner, duly authorized in writing to assist the Architect and Engineer in supervision of the work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.05)

q: Under the same Article, if the Owner fails to pay the Contractor any sum awarded by arbitration within a certain period, per Sec. 27(d), the Contractor may suspend or terminate the Contract (with 15 days' notice) if that failure exceeds how many days after the arbitration award?
n: Art. 27(d) allows the Contractor this right if the Owner fails to pay any sum within thirty (30) days after its award by arbitration. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 27(d))
scenario: A Contractor governed by UAP Doc. 301 is evaluating whether recent events on its project give it grounds under Art. 27 to suspend work or terminate the Contract, each requiring the appropriate written notice period.

q: The Architect issues a Certificate of Completion for a building project. Per Sec. 20.12, what is the maximum length, unless otherwise expressly named in the Contract, of the "Period of Making Good of Known Defects or Faults," counted from the date of that Certificate?
n: Sec. 20.12 defines the Period of Making Good of Known Defects or Faults as not more than sixty (60) calendar days from the date of issue of the Certificate of Completion, unless the Contract expressly states otherwise. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.12)

q: How many copies of complete catalog data must the Contractor furnish for every manufactured item of equipment, under Sec. 9.02?
n: Sec. 9.02 (Equipment Approval Data) requires the Contractor to furnish three copies of complete catalog data for every manufactured item of equipment used in the work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 9, Sec. 9.02)

q: Which UAP Doc. 301 term describes "the notice published by the Owner or the invitations issued to prospective bidders, giving information as to the nature of the proposed project ... date of bidding, and estimated cost"?
n: Sec. 1.15 defines the Advertisement or Invitation to Bid in these terms. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.15)

q: Under Sec. 30.01, who must the Contractor designate on the work, whose duty is the prevention of accidents and damage to the Owner's property and adjoining property, and to whom must this designation be reported?
o: A responsible member of the Contractor's organization, reported to the Architect
The Contractor's Surety, reported to the Owner
A licensed safety officer, reported to the DOLE
A third-party insurance adjuster, reported to the Board of Arbitration
n: Sec. 30.01 requires the Contractor to designate a responsible member of his organization for accident/damage prevention and to report that person's name and position to the Architect. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 30, Sec. 30.01)

q: Under the same facts, a delay caused by a typhoon (a recognized Act of God) occurs on-site. Per Sec. 21.04(a), within how many days from the occurrence of the delay must the Contractor file its request for a time extension?
n: Sec. 21.04(a) requires the Contractor to file the necessary request for extension within fifteen (15) days from the occurrence of the qualifying delay (e.g., Act of God, Owner-caused delay, strikes). (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 21, Sec. 21.04(a))
scenario: A building Contractor receives its Notice to Proceed (NTP) dated March 1 for a project governed by UAP Doc. 301. Various contract-administration deadlines under Art. 21 (Time of Completion) must now be tracked from that date.

q: If the Architect fails to condemn or reject bad or inferior materials at the time of delivery, does this failure, per Sec. 10.07(b), imply the Owner has accepted those materials?
o: Yes, silence is always deemed acceptance
No — failure or neglect to reject bad materials does not imply acceptance if the defect is discovered any time before final acceptance of the work and release of the Contractor
No, but only the Owner (not the Architect) may later reject materials
Yes, but only if 30 days have passed
n: Sec. 10.07(b) provides that the Architect's failure to reject bad/inferior materials does not constitute acceptance if discovered before final acceptance of the work and release of the Contractor. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 10, Sec. 10.07(b))

q: The "listing of the different parts of the work indicating in each part the corresponding value in materials and labor, including an allowance for profit and overhead" is defined in the General Conditions as the:
o: Breakdown of Work and Corresponding Value
n: Sec. 1.24 defines the Breakdown of Work and Corresponding Value in these terms; it later becomes the basis for all Requests for Payment under Art. 22. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.24)

q: On the same Php 8,000,000 project, after Final Acceptance, the Owner releases the Performance and Payment Bonds. Per Sec. 31.04, the Contractor must furnish a Guarantee Bond worth how much, and covering what period?
o: Php 2,400,000 (30%), for one year commencing from the date of acceptance
n: Sec. 31.04 requires a Guarantee Bond of 30% of the Total Contract Cost (30% x Php 8,000,000 = Php 2,400,000), for a period of one year from the date of acceptance. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 31, Sec. 31.04)
scenario: A Contractor has been awarded a Php 8,000,000 building contract under UAP Doc. 301. Before signing the Contract, it must post the bonds required under Art. 31, and later replace them per that Article's sequence.

q: Under Sec. 21.04(d), if no schedule or agreement exists stating when drawings will be furnished, no claim for delay due to failure to furnish drawings is allowed until how long after demand for such drawings?
n: Sec. 21.04(d) bars a delay claim for failure to furnish drawings until two weeks after demand for such drawings (and unless the claim is reasonable). (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 21, Sec. 21.04(d))

q: Per Art. 13, manufactured articles must be applied, installed, connected, erected, used, cleaned and conditioned in accordance with:
o: Whatever is fastest to complete the work
Manufacturer's printed directions, unless specified to the contrary
The Contractor's own field practice, regardless of manufacturer instructions
n: Art. 13 (Manufacturer's Directions) requires compliance with manufacturer's printed directions unless the Specifications state otherwise. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 13)

q: Under Sec. 1.34, unless the Contract states otherwise, the words "approved," "directed," and "acceptable" (or words of like import) mean approved, directed, or acceptable to whom?
n: Sec. 1.34 provides that such words mean approved/directed by or acceptable to the Architect, unless the Contract stipulates otherwise. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.34)

q: Under Sec. 32.01, who must the Owner give a list of, prior to the start of construction, so that they may be covered by insurance with corresponding coverage amounts?
o: Members of the Board of Arbitration
Personnel assigned to the project (under the Owner's employ or services) who need insurance coverage
n: Sec. 32.01 requires the Owner and Architect to give, prior to construction start, a list of project personnel needing insurance coverage, with the amount of coverage. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 32, Sec. 32.01)

q: The same project later reaches 55% completion, and a new Request for Payment for additional work accomplished is submitted. Per Sec. 22.02, what retention now applies to this and subsequent billings?
o: 10% retention continues on the full amount
No further retention is made on the balance of the Contract, since 50% has been exceeded
Retention is doubled to make up for the earlier grace period
n: Sec. 22.02 provides that when 50% of the Contract has been accomplished, no further retention shall be made on the balance of the Contract. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.02)
scenario: A Contractor is billing progress payments on a Php 10,000,000 building contract governed by UAP Doc. 301. At the time of a given billing, the Contract's cumulative percentage of completion determines what retention rules and payment procedures apply.

q: Under Sec. 15.11 (Temporary or Trial Usage), if the Owner makes temporary or trial use of equipment before final completion and written acceptance by the Architect, is this use construed as the Architect's acceptance of the work?
o: Only if it lasts more than 30 days
Only if the Owner pays an additional fee
No — temporary or trial usage before final completion and written acceptance shall not be construed as evidence of the Architect's acceptance
n: Sec. 15.11 expressly states temporary or trial usage is not evidence of the Architect's acceptance of the work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 15, Sec. 15.11)

q: A Contractor notices a discrepancy between the Drawings and actual site conditions but proceeds with the work without reporting it to the Architect. Under Sec. 2.03(b), at whose risk is this work performed?
o: Shared equally between Owner and Contractor
n: Sec. 2.03(b) provides that discrepancies must be immediately reported to the Architect/Engineer, and any work involving such discrepancies is done at the Contractor's risk. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 2, Sec. 2.03(b))

q: A dispute over a question of fact arises under the Contract. Per Sec. 33.04(b)-(c), whose decision on such factual disputes is final and conclusive upon the parties (unless the Contract specifically provides otherwise)?
n: Sec. 33.04(b)-(c) makes the Architect's decision on questions of fact final and conclusive on the parties, except as otherwise specifically provided. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 33, Sec. 33.04(b)-(c))

q: Within how many days from the Architect's approval of a Request for Payment (or issuance of a Certificate of Payment) must the Owner pay the certified amount, per Sec. 22.07?
n: Sec. 22.07 requires the Owner to pay within fifteen (15) days from the date of approval of a Request for Payment or issuance of a Certificate of Payment. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.07)

q: Under Art. 17 (Protection of Adjacent Property and Existing Utilities), if an existing utility is damaged due to the Contractor's negligence or fault, who bears the repair cost?
o: The Contractor, at his own expense
Split equally between Owner and Contractor
n: Sec. 17.02 (Existing Utilities) places the cost of repairing utilities damaged by the Contractor's negligence squarely on the Contractor. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 17, Sec. 17.02)

q: Where figures are given on the Drawings but conflict with what would be obtained by scaling the drawing, Sec. 3.02 provides that:
o: The Architect must always resolve this by re-issuing the drawing
The Contractor may choose whichever is more convenient
The stated figures are to be followed in preference to measurements by scale
n: Sec. 3.02 (Coordination of Drawings and Specifications) provides that where figures are given, they govern over scaled measurements. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 3, Sec. 3.02)

q: Per Art. 34(a), the Architect acts as the Owner's representative during construction, with authority to act on the Owner's behalf:
o: Only if the Owner is physically absent from the country
Only to the extent expressly provided in the Contract Documents or otherwise in writing, shown to the Contractor
Only for design matters, never for financial matters
n: Art. 34(a) limits the Architect's authority to act for the Owner to what is expressly provided in the Contract Documents or otherwise given in writing and shown to the Contractor. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 34(a))

q: Before final payment, Sec. 22.11(g) requires the Contractor to submit a Guarantee Bond equivalent to what percentage of the Contract Price, covering what period after Final Acceptance?
o: 10% of the Contract Price, for two years
15% of the Contract Price, for six months
50% of the Contract Price, for one year
30% of the Contract Price, for one year after Final Acceptance
n: Sec. 22.11(g) requires a Guarantee Bond equal to 30% of the Contract Price, covering a period of one year after Final Acceptance of the work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.11(g))

q: On re-examination of questioned work ordered by the Architect, if the uncovered work is found to be defective due to the Contractor's fault, Sec. 20.03(b) provides that the cost of examination:
o: Is charged to the Architect's professional fee
n: Sec. 20.03(b) provides that if re-examined work is found not in accordance with the Contract Documents, the Contractor bears the cost. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.03(b))

q: How many copies of shop or setting drawings, templates, patterns and models must the Contractor submit under Sec. 5.01, and at whose expense are they prepared?
o: Five copies, at the Sub-contractor's expense
Three copies, at the Owner's expense
One copy, at the Architect's expense
Two copies, at the Contractor's own expense
n: Sec. 5.01 requires the Contractor to prepare, at his own expense, two copies of shop or setting drawings, templates, patterns and models for the Architect's review. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 5, Sec. 5.01)

q: Per Sec. 36.01, Project Representatives, Resident Architects, Resident Engineers, or Construction Inspectors stationed on a project are typically:
o: Recommended by the Architect and employed by the Owner, to assist the Architect and Engineers in general supervision
Appointed by the Board of Arbitration
Independent consultants with no reporting relationship to the Architect
Employed by the Contractor, to protect his own interests
n: Sec. 36.01 describes these on-site technical personnel as recommended by the Architect and employed by the Owner, assisting in general supervision and direction of the work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 36, Sec. 36.01)

q: Under Art. 23, the Owner reserves what right in connection with the project?
o: The right to dismiss the Architect at will
The right to withhold the Notice to Proceed indefinitely
The right to let other (separate) contracts in connection with the work
The right to unilaterally reduce the Contract Price
n: Art. 23 (Sec. 23.01) reserves to the Owner the right to let other contracts in connection with the same work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 23, Sec. 23.01)

q: Still on the same Php 20,000,000 contract, the Owner and Contractor instead agree to value a change using unit prices already stipulated in the Contract. Per Sec. 20.07(d)(2), this method may be used provided the extra or credit does not exceed what percentage of the original contract value of the particular work involved?
n: Sec. 20.07(d)(2) allows valuation by stipulated unit prices provided the extra or credit does not exceed 25% of the original contract value of that particular work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.07(d)(2))
scenario: A Contractor is executing a Php 20,000,000 lump-sum building contract under UAP Doc. 301. During construction, several quantity and cost adjustments become necessary and are being evaluated against the General Conditions' rules on changes, extra work, and time extensions.

q: A Contractor fails to visit the project site before bidding and later claims extra compensation and time extension because of site conditions it did not anticipate. Under Sec. 6.02, is this claim valid?
o: Yes, but only if the Owner agrees in writing
Yes, ignorance of site conditions always justifies compensation
No — the Contractor is expected to have visited the site and made his own estimates before bidding; no extra compensation or time extension is given for his own negligence or inadvertence
No, but only if the site is outside Metro Manila
n: Sec. 6.02 (Site Conditions) places the burden on the Contractor to inspect the site before bidding; no extra compensation/extension is granted for the Contractor's own negligence. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 6, Sec. 6.02)

q: Which General Conditions document is described as "printed documents stipulating the procedural and administrative aspects of the contract" — i.e., the very document being discussed in this reviewer topic?
n: Sec. 1.19 defines the General Conditions themselves (UAP Doc. 301) as the printed documents stipulating the procedural and administrative aspects of the contract. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.19)

q: Per Sec. 26.02(c), a Sub-contractor's claim to the Contractor for extras, time extension, or delay damages follows the same procedure as the Contractor's claims upon the Owner, EXCEPT that the time allowed for making claims for extra cost is:
o: Fifteen days, same as the Contractor
n: Sec. 26.02(c) shortens the Sub-contractor's claim period for extra cost to one week, unlike the Contractor's 15-day period under Sec. 20.08. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 26, Sec. 26.02(c))

q: If the Contractor believes an Architect's instruction involves extra cost, Sec. 20.08 requires written notice to the Architect within how many days after receipt of the instruction, and before what point must this notice be given?
o: 15 days; before proceeding to execute the work (except in emergencies)
5 days; only after the work is finished
30 days; after completing the work in question
n: Sec. 20.08 requires written notice within 15 days after receipt of the instruction and, in any event, before proceeding to execute the work (except emergencies under Sec. 20.05). (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.08)

q: Under Sec. 7.04(b), within how many hours of discovering a deviation from the Drawings must a licensed surveyor certify that deviation to the Architect?
n: Sec. 7.04(b) requires the surveyor to certify any deviation from the Drawings to the Architect within 24 hours of its discovery. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 7, Sec. 7.04(b))

q: Which defined term refers to "anyone having a direct Contract with the Contractor who acts for or in behalf of the Contractor in executing any part of the Contract," but excludes a party who merely furnishes materials without labor?
n: Sec. 1.07 defines the Sub-Contractor this way, expressly excluding a materials-only supplier. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.07)

q: Under Art. 28, before the Owner may terminate the Contract for sufficient cause (e.g., the Contractor's insolvency or failure to pay sub-contractors), how many days' written notice must be given to the Contractor and his Surety?
n: Art. 28 requires the Owner to give the Contractor (and Surety, if any) fifteen (15) days' written notice before terminating the Contract, upon the Architect's certification that sufficient cause exists. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 28)

q: Per Sec. 20.13, if a known defect is discovered as a result of an inspection made just before the 60-day Period of Making Good expires, within how many additional days after the period's expiration must the Contractor still make the correction?
n: Sec. 20.13 requires the Contractor to make good known defects within sixty days after issuance of the Certificate of Completion, or within fifteen days after the period's expiration if the defect was found by a pre-expiration inspection. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.13)

q: Unless otherwise specified, how many samples of a material must the Contractor submit for approval under Sec. 10.02(a), and in what form must the request for approval be transmitted per Sec. 10.02(d)?
o: Three samples; letter of transmittal in triplicate
Two samples; letter of transmittal in duplicate
Five samples; no transmittal letter required
n: Sec. 10.02(a) requires three samples unless otherwise specified, and Sec. 10.02(d) requires a letter of transmittal in triplicate to accompany all sets of samples. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 10, Secs. 10.02(a) and (d))

q: "Additional information on Contract Documents issued to bidders before date of bidding" is the definition of which term?
n: Sec. 1.16 defines the Bid Bulletin as additional information on Contract Documents issued to bidders before the bidding date. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.16)

q: Per Sec. 30.02, is the Owner responsible for the death, disease, or injury of the Contractor's own employees or laborers, or for damage to the Contractor's plant or materials?
o: Yes, the Owner is always responsible
Only for injuries occurring during Owner-directed emergency work
No — the Owner shall not be responsible for these; all such damages are the responsibility of the Contractor
Only if the Owner's own negligence caused the injury
n: Sec. 30.02 disclaims Owner responsibility for injuries to the Contractor's own workforce and damage to the Contractor's plant/materials, placing that responsibility on the Contractor. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 30, Sec. 30.02)

q: Continuing the scenario, the Contractor anticipates it will need Owner-furnished materials for a later phase of work. Per Sec. 21.04(a) (proviso), how many days before the materials are actually needed must the Contractor make a written request for them, in order to later claim a valid time extension for the Owner's failure to furnish them?
n: The proviso to Sec. 21.04(a) requires a written request for Owner-furnished materials/information at least ten (10) days before they are actually needed, or no extension is granted for the Owner's alleged failure to furnish them. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 21, Sec. 21.04(a))
scenario: A building Contractor receives its Notice to Proceed (NTP) dated March 1 for a project governed by UAP Doc. 301. Various contract-administration deadlines under Art. 21 (Time of Completion) must now be tracked from that date.

q: No extension of time or substitution of materials shall be allowed for delays in imported materials, fixtures, appliances and equipment, per Sec. 10.08, when the cause is:
o: A change ordered by the Architect
Negligence or inadvertence of the Contractor
n: Sec. 10.08 provides no time extension or material substitution is allowed for delay due to the Contractor's own negligence or inadvertence in arranging for imported materials. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 10, Sec. 10.08)

q: Per Sec. 1.25, a "Written Notice" under the General Conditions is valid when it is:
o: Verbally communicated and later confirmed by telephone
Sent by any form of electronic mail
Delivered in person or sent by registered mail to the last known business address of the individual, firm or corporation
Posted on the project bulletin board only
n: Sec. 1.25 defines Written Notice as information delivered in person or sent by registered mail to the last known business address. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.25)

q: Per Sec. 31.04, how many months after Final Acceptance of the work must elapse before the Performance and Payment Bonds are released by the Owner (and only after the Guarantee Bond is furnished)?
n: Sec. 31.04 provides that the Performance and Payment Bonds are released after the expiration of two (2) months from Final Acceptance of the work, and only after the Guarantee Bond has been furnished. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 31, Sec. 31.04)

q: Under Sec. 21.05 (Liquidated Damages), payment of liquidated damages by the Contractor for late completion is characterized in the General Conditions as:
o: An advance on the final billing
A discretionary gift to the Owner
n: Sec. 21.05 expressly states the payment is made as liquidated damages, and not by way of penalty, and may be deducted by the Owner from any sum due the Contractor. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 21, Sec. 21.05)

q: Under Sec. 14.02, what is the Contractor prohibited from doing to any part of the structure?
o: Allowing workers to smoke anywhere on site
Loading or permitting any part of the structure to be loaded with a weight that will endanger its safety
n: Sec. 14.02 (Safeguard for Structure) prohibits the Contractor from loading or permitting the structure to be loaded with weight endangering its safety. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 14, Sec. 14.02)

q: Local Laws, as defined in Sec. 1.28 of the General Conditions, cover:
o: All laws, ordinances and other governmental regulations applicable to the project and its undertaking
Only national laws, excluding city/municipal ordinances
n: Sec. 1.28 defines Local Laws broadly as all laws, ordinances, and governmental regulations applicable to the project. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.28)
